name: h1-cost
assumptions: Tokens are pi's own estimate, characters over four (pi-coding-agent estimateTokens); the high estimate counts three characters per token (token_scale 4/3) for JSON, ids and non-English text.
The scripted cassettes fix one memory read and one answer per session; the high estimate lets a live model make two more reads, each repeating the session so far and a read as large as the first.

Memory per read on the full set: each checkpoint's own question as the query (GateMem, research/results/h1-c4-walk.json); every entry of a case, or what the preset admits under C5 (MEM-INV-Bench, research/results/h1-mem-inv-admission.json). Tokens per item are the fixture reads'.
The GateMem prompt moves from the fixture checkpoints' size to the full set's mean per item kind; the MEM-INV-Bench prompt is the fixture's (one system prompt, short tasks).
Answers and the judge's verdict are as long as the scripted ones; a live answer may be longer, which the high estimate's token scale covers only in part.
The runner asks for thinking off; the high estimate adds 1,024 reasoning output tokens per answer call for every model the catalogue marks as reasoning, and none for the judge (GPT-4o).
The judge runs once per GateMem session (low) or three times (high, upstream's three attempts); HTTP retries are not counted.
MEM-INV-Bench's 8 agent notes cost their recorded size (low) or their 300-token limit (high).
No prompt caching, batch discount or provider minimum is assumed; prices are list prices from the catalogue, not a quote.
